children.heading: CardioTrack CT-200 Home Blood Pressure Monitor — Technical & User Manual
children.body: CardioTrack CT-200 Home Blood Pressure Monitor — Technical & User Manual

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: The CardioTrack CT-200 is an oscillometric, upper-arm blood pressure

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: monitor intended for home use by adult users. It measures systolic

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: pressure, diastolic pressure, and pulse rate, and stores up to 200

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: readings across two user profiles.

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: The CT-200 is intended to non-invasively measure blood pressure and

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: pulse rate in adults with an arm circumference of 22–42 cm. It is not

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: intended for use on neonates, infants, or pregnant users, and is not a

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: diagnostic device — readings should be interpreted by a qualified

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: clinician.

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: The device should not be used on the arm ipsilateral to a mastectomy,

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: on limbs with an active intravenous line, or on users with severe

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: arrhythmia without clinician guidance, since oscillometric measurement

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: can be unreliable in these cases.

children.heading: Table on page 2
children.body:
Parameter | Value
Measurement | method | Oscillometric
Pressure | range | 0–299 | mmHg

raw_rows: Power source 4x AA batteries or 6V DC adapter

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: Under typical use (three measurements per day), four AA alkaline

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: batteries provide approximately 250 measurement cycles before

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: requiring replacement — revised downward from earlier estimates after

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: extended field testing. The device displays a low ‐ battery icon once

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: remaining capacity falls below 10%.

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: The standard cuff supplied with the CT ‐ 200 fits arm circumferences of

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: 22–32 cm. A separate large cuff (part number CT200 ‐ LC) is available for

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: 32–42 cm and must be ordered separately; using the standard cuff

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: outside its rated range will produce inaccurate readings.

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: Press and hold the power button for one second to power on the device.

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: Use the profile button to select User 1 or User 2 before beginning a

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: measurement; readings are stored against whichever profile is active at

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: the time of measurement.

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: On starting a measurement, the device inflates the cuff to an initial target

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: of 180 mmHg. If the user's pulse is not detected by 180 mmHg, the

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: device inflates in 30 mmHg increments up to a maximum of 299 mmHg

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: before aborting with an error. Deflation occurs in controlled steps of

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: approximately 3 mmHg to capture oscillometric pulse data. Increment

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: size was reduced from the original 40 mmHg to improve pulse-detection

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: reliability in field testing.

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: To conserve battery, the CT ‐ 200 automatically powers off after 60

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: seconds of inactivity on the home screen, and after 3 minutes of

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: inactivity if a measurement screen is left open without starting a reading.

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: After a completed measurement, the device displays systolic pressure,

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: diastolic pressure, and pulse rate simultaneously, along with a

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: classification indicator (see 2.1, 4.3 for related specifications and alarm

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: thresholds) based on the most recent joint clinical guidance available at

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: time of manufacture.

children.heading: List Item
children.body: Normal: systolic < 120 and diastolic < 80

children.heading: List Item
children.body: Elevated: systolic 120–129 and diastolic < 80

children.heading: List Item
children.body: Hypertension Stage 1: systolic 130–139 or diastolic 80–89

children.heading: List Item
children.body: Hypertension Stage 2: systolic ≥ 140 or diastolic ≥ 90

children.heading: List Item
children.body: Hypertensive Crisis: systolic > 180 or diastolic > 120 — device

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: recommends seeking immediate medical attention

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: If cuff pressure exceeds 299 mmHg at any point, or exceeds 300 mmHg

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: for longer than 3 seconds due to sensor fault, the device immediately

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: triggers an emergency deflation valve, halting inflation and venting the

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: cuff within 2 seconds, independent of the main firmware control loop.

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: The device does not sound an audible alarm for elevated readings by

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: default; audible alarms are limited to the E1–E6 error conditions above

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: and are user ‐ configurable in the settings menu, except for E3

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: (overpressure), which cannot be silenced for safety reasons.

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: The CT ‐ 200 stores up to 100 readings per user profile in non ‐ volatile

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: memory. When storage is full, the oldest reading for that profile is

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: overwritten automatically; there is no user ‐ facing warning before this

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: occurs.

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: The device can pair with the CardioTrack companion app via Bluetooth

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: Low Energy. Readings sync automatically when the app is open and the

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: device is within range; there is no manual "sync now" trigger in firmware

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: version 1.x.

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: Starting with firmware 1.4, the companion app supports exporting stored

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: readings as a CSV file containing timestamp, profile, systolic, diastolic,

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: pulse, and classification columns. Export requires the device to have

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: completed at least one successful Bluetooth sync in the current session.

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: Wipe the device body and cuff exterior with a soft, dry cloth or one lightly

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: dampened with water. Do not submerge the device or cuff, and do not

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: use alcohol, solvents, or abrasive cleaners on the display.

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: Anthropic recommends professional recalibration every 2 years or after

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: any drop or significant impact. The device does not perform

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: self ‐ calibration; there is no field calibration procedure available to end

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: users.

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: If a code from Section 4.2 appears and persists after following the

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: on ‐ screen retry prompt twice, users should discontinue use and contact

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: CardioTrack support rather than attempting further self ‐ diagnosis,

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: particularly for E5, which indicates an internal sensor fault.

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: Inconsistent readings between measurements are most commonly

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: caused by cuff mispositioning, talking or moving during measurement, or

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: measuring within 30 minutes of exercise, caffeine, or smoking; the

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: manual recommends resting quietly for 5 minutes before remeasuring.

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: The CT ‐ 200 is classified as a Class II medical device under applicable

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: regulations for non ‐ invasive blood pressure monitors and has been

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: validated against relevant clinical accuracy standards for oscillometric

children.heading: Paragraph
children.body: devices.
